purpose: Map ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals (27 state releases, 54 dataset sections) back to the government services it was scraped from; test which are live, queryable by bbox, CORS-open and geo-fenced; and measure which Indian target cities each dataset covers.

method.releases: gh api repos/ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals/releases; scraper scripts in ramSeraph/staging_opendata maps/* and ramSeraph/indianopenmaps worker/src/routes/listing.json
method.cityCoverage: DuckDB httpfs over the remote GeoParquet (row-group bbox pruning): count of parcels whose bbox intersects a +-0.01 deg box (about 2.2 km square) around each target city centre. Zero counts omitted. Rural village datasets often exclude city cores, so a WUP centre point with 0-5 parcels means only fringe coverage.
method.reachability: one tiny request per endpoint from the laptop with Origin https://urbangametheory.xyz; timeouts re-tested via check-host.net nodes in1/de1/us1/sg1 (check-host connect timeout is about 3 s).
method.tiles: tiles.json plus one decoded tile per route at its max zoom (mapbox_vector_tile).
method.targets: world-parcels/registry.json (countryCode IN) + queue-top200.json (iso2 IN) + queue-india-africa.json (India), 223 cities; app ids from frontend/js/city-config.js.

indianopenmapsTileService.cors: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on tiles.json and tiles (all 55 cadastral routes)
indianopenmapsTileService.maxZoom: 11-16 by dataset (most 13-15); no overzoom beyond max
indianopenmapsTileService.backing: Cloudflare Worker reading the PMTiles/mosaic assets of the GitHub releases server-side; the PMTiles themselves are only on GitHub release URLs (no CORS), so direct PMTiles range reads from a browser are not possible.
indianopenmapsTileService.identifiers: MVT feature ids are absent (0); each route lists a promoteId property for MapLibre (e.g. HRSAC uq, TRAC OBJECTID_12, NCSCM OBJECTID, KGIS OBJECTID). Several routes have none (MRSAC, MPSSDI, JSAC, Odisha, Bhuvan Kerala/SISDP).
indianopenmapsTileService.geometry: Clipped at tile edges with a buffer (rings extend past the tile extent). At max zoom simple parcels keep their vertices (HRSAC median 6 in parquet vs 7 in tile) but detailed ones are simplified (NCSCM Maharashtra median 14 vs 10). A parcel can be split across tiles; tiles are not a source of exact parcel geometry.
indianopenmapsTileService.status: Third-party, unofficial, "not-so-open" path; snapshot dates 2024-11 to 2026-03; no SLA.

liveService.type: GeoServer WMS (namespace cadastral:*, ~140 district layers e.g. cadastral:Kamrup_M_Cad_sisdp_p2, Visakhapatnam_Cad_sisdp_p2, Krishna_Cad_sisdp_p2, Panipat_Cad_sisdp_p2, KL_Cad, WB_cad, tn_cad)
liveService.reachability: 200 from laptop and all check-host nodes (capabilities 7.5 MB, slow)
liveService.notes: The GeoRSS GetMap route ramSeraph used is now refused ("Creating maps using application/rss+xml is not allowed") and WFS is disabled. Only rendered WMS images and point GetFeatureInfo remain; no CORS, so even GFI needs a relay.

problems: Most state services the releases were scraped from are now dead or India-only: APSAC, MPSSDI, WB AMRUT, Goa bhunakshawms, all NCOG/BISAG-N hosts, J&K LRIS proxy, Bharatmaps webgis1, NBSS and the old tgracgis host did not answer from any check-host node, including India.
Bhuvan disabled WFS and the GeoRSS GetMap format that ramSeraph used, so Assam, Chhattisgarh, Kerala and West Bengal Bhuvan parcels are now only raster WMS.

Rural cadastral datasets miss city cores: Hyderabad (TRAC 1), Pune (MRSAC 3), Nagpur (MRSAC 1), Bengaluru (KGIS 90 at the fringe), Darbhanga (2), Bhopal (MP about 170). City-centre counts understate them as city sources.
Registry/queue data issue: WUP 11569 is named "Cape Town" but sits at 20.465,85.879 (Cuttack, Odisha); the Odisha4kgeo count of 16,098 belongs to Cuttack.
Some release parquets contain garbage geometries (PunjabGIS and Goa Bhunaksha first rows near 0 N 70 E; HRSAC and PunjabGIS row groups spanning half of India), which inflate row-group extents.
mapservice.gov.in (Matribhoomi) chains to the new Let's Encrypt Root YR; older trust stores (Homebrew Python) fail TLS verification.
NCSCM plot labels (Plot/Survey_Number + Village) are not unique keys; HRSAC uq, KGIS KGISCadastralID, MP ulpin/parcel_id, J&K ULPIN and Goa pniu are the only strong native ids seen.
Lakshadweep and Andaman NCSCM layers are no longer listed in the current CZMP services; CZMP_Odisha19 has no survey-plot layer.

NCOG Gujarat and NCSCM Gujarat return identical counts near Surat (249), Bhavnagar (107) and Jamnagar (97), so the NCOG Gujarat layer likely embeds the coastal CZMP plots there rather than independent revenue maps.
The KGIS parquet failed once with a ZSTD decompression error on a range read and succeeded on retry.
